summary.text: A vector space is a set whose elements, called vectors, can be added together and scaled by numbers called scalars, following rules known as the vector axioms.
Vector spaces generalize Euclidean vectors, which model physical quantities such as forces and velocity that have both a magnitude and a direction.
Every vector space has a dimension, roughly the number of independent directions, and all bases of the space have that same size.

facts.label: Core operations
facts.value: Adding vectors and scaling them by numbers called scalars

facts.label: Meaning of dimension
facts.value: Roughly, the number of independent directions in the space

facts.label: Infinite example
facts.value: Polynomial rings are countably infinite-dimensional vector spaces

facts.label: What a basis is
facts.value: Linearly independent elements that span the whole space

items.prompt: You take a few vectors, scale each one, and add the scaled copies together in every possible way. What do all those results form?
items.explain: The span of a set is the set of all linear combinations of its elements, and it is the smallest linear subspace containing them.

items.prompt: In a set of vectors, one turns out to be a mix of scaled copies of the others added together. What does that tell you about the set?

options.label: It is a basis for the space

items.explain: Linear independence means no element can be written as a linear combination of the others, so this set fails it.

items.prompt: Which collection of vectors both spans the space and has no member that is a combination of the others?
items.explain: A basis is a subset whose elements are linearly independent and span the vector space.

items.prompt: Two students choose different bases for the same vector space and count the vectors in theirs. What do they find?

options.label: The counts can differ by any amount
The larger basis is always the better one
Both counts are the same number, the dimension
Only one of them can have a valid basis

items.explain: All bases of a vector space have the same cardinality, which is called the dimension.

items.prompt: A non-empty subset W of a vector space has this property: adding two elements of W, or scaling one, always stays in W. What is W called?
items.explain: A subset closed under vector addition and scalar multiplication is a linear subspace.

items.prompt: Why do physicists describe a force with a vector rather than a single number?

options.label: A single number cannot be negative
Forces are always measured in whole numbers
Vectors are quicker to write down
A force has a direction as well as a size

items.explain: Euclidean vectors model quantities such as forces and velocity, which have not only a magnitude but also a direction.
